Patch Set 1:

(2 comments)

AI code review results below, please doublecheck

The fix itself looks right - the memset() covers every branch of the if/else chain, including the one with no terminal else, and both callers (lustre_msg_set_jobinfo() and vvp_io_init()) pass a real sizeof(), so zeroing @joblen rather than @len is safe. A couple of small points inline.

The message describes a concrete reproducer (jobid_var naming an absent variable plus a process whose comm matches a reserved prefix, checked against obdfilter.*.job_stats), but no test is added. Would a sanity.sh case next to test_205b work - set jobid_var to a variable that is not in the environment, run I/O from a copy of dd named to match one of the jobid_name_is_valid() prefixes, and assert job_stats gains no escaped \\xHH entry? verify_yaml() in test_205g would not catch it, since a garbage jobid is escaped and quoted and stays valid YAML.

commit.subject: LU-20614 obdclass: always define the jobid buffer
commit.message:
LU-20614 obdclass: always define the jobid buffer

lustre_get_jobid() is documented to return %0 on success, but returns
0 without storing anything in @jobid when obd_jobid_var names an
environment variable and jobid_name_is_valid() rejects current->comm.
The chain has long had no terminal else; what changed is that the
zeroed staging buffer whose contents were copied out wholesale went
away, and the on-stack job_info below it arrived in the same commit.

So the tail is now kernel stack on the wire: vvp_io_init() passes
ji_jobid from an uninitialized struct job_info, memcpy()s the struct
into lli_jobinfo, and lustre_msg_set_jobinfo() copies all 32 bytes
into pb_jobid unconditionally. Zero @jobid once on entry, covering
every path, and terminate it at the start of jobid_interpret_string()
so the expansion is defined for its own sake. While there, correct the
environment entry, which claimed the lookup is skipped only for Lustre
and kernel service threads.
